To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The predictive power of firm level equity price and volatility is significant in a number of developed countries and is related to the business cycle position; 2) The predictive power is related to selected balance-sheet items; 3) The economic VaR based on firm-level equity price and volatility information is related to selected macroeconomic indicators and to the business cycle.
Stock market information at firm level improves the predictability of real economic activity, both in the short and long run, in a large number of countries.

(i) the return and volatility of individual firm-level equity prices improve the predictability for future IP changes of the aggregate economy in four economic areas (United States, United Kingdom, Germany and Japan), (ii) this is true for the domestic as well as the foreign firms, (iii) the sectoral classification also matters, and (iv) balance sheet features are relevant to distinguish firms that can anticipate future IP developments from those that do no help in this aim.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between stock market firm-level information and real economic activity.
the role of firm-level stock market information in forecasting business cycle fluctuations in the United States and in four other economic areas.
the role of firm-level information for macroeconomic forecasting, with a particular focus on the business cycle and the financial cycle, and with its potential use for macro-prudential purposes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the information on the equity market, and in particular on firm level equity prices, can be a useful complement to the information on the aggregate equity market.
the stock market is not just an indicator of the business cycle, but also of the future business cycle.

1) the predictive power of stock market information on future economic activity is related to the position of the economy in its own business cycle, 2) the predictive power is not only related to the position in the business cycle but also to structural features of the firm, and 3) the predictive power varies over time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stock market firm-level information is a key to understand the aggregate economic dynamics.
we find that the stock market information is a key factor in the prediction of the real economy.
stock market firm-level information improves business cycle predictability, especially in countries that have a large number of firms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
stock markets can provide useful information to predict business cycle developments.
stock market firm-level information is a valuable source of information for the business cycle.
the information contained in the stock market is not equally distributed across firms and across time.
